items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: all these arrangements by people like Sam Nistico

ctx.x: Especially most of the colleges, academics and reading -- there are some excellent big bands as an ensemble, but most of the soloists were lacking because they probably hadn't had the experience of playing where you could just really blow.

Now any of these bands, as good as they are -- all these arrangements by people like Sam Nistico; and some of these arrangers that seem to be so busy now writing for Maynard Ferguson and Woodie Herman and Buddy Rich-- this stuff is absolutely good. But I just don't see it doing the job that it should do to really lift that big band thing up where the bottom fell out, after Kenton, because the best is still Count Basie -- to have a big

audience and still play good big band music. Although these other guys are good, they are not important enough, they haven't come through -- Maynard Ferguson's band or Buddy Rich's band is fine for drum leader. That's good enough, but I mean for a big band, you know, regardless of the leader, the big jazz band, to carry on where Basie and Duke left and of course, when I say Benny Goodman, that's Fletcher Henderson sound -- Fletcher Henderson originated the Goodman style, you know.
